rounds.text: Super Spinning Mills Ltd is deeply under-appreciated because it trades at a steep discount to its underlying assets, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.69x based on a share price of ₹ 6.36 against a book value of ₹ 9.20 [E1]. This deep asset discount is further highlighted when compared to the broader sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 1.26x, leaving the company priced at just 0.65x relative to that benchmark [E5]. Furthermore, despite broader operational headwinds, the company generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 2 Cr in Mar 2016 [E23], alongside a substantial free cash flow of Rs 33 Cr in the same period [E24]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of -6.40% over the past five years [E45], compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has dropped by -21% [E11], and the return on equity stands at -43.0% [E8]. However, with a market capitalisation of only ₹ 35.0 Cr [E2] and the stock sitting comfortably at just 37% of the way up its 52-week range [E4], the current valuation fails to credit the tangible asset backing and cash generation capacity present in the business [E1, E24].
